This week note covers the week of 13th–20th July.


Aliens vs. The Fish

Since I’m writing this week note so late, I’ll throw in an extra day for free.
Last week was the week of birthdays. Both my wife and our now 4yo A had their birthdays, and the whole week was spent in celebrations. For A’s birthday, we went to the Aquarium Paradise, probably the largest aquarium in Bengaluru. A had a lot of fun looking at all the fish and other sea creatures. The photo above is from the aquarium, which had a weird theme of Egypt × Aliens × Pirates × Mermaids. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

This week note covers the week of 6th–12th July.

Last Day of Summer

Yes, I was there at the foot of the Eiffel Tower 9 years ago, and yes, I took this photo. I visited Paris on my way to Berlin for EuroClojure 2017, where I talked about Moving People with Clojure. It feels like a lifetime ago, maybe it was.
Today is a lazy day in sort of a contemplative way. I really did not feel like writing this week note, but this week is going to be busy so it’s now or never.
Last week went too quickly I think. I was busy with work, with three hours spent in commute every day, with my drum classes, and with tinkering on this website. Everyone in my family is doing well now health-wise, and I hope it stays this way. This week has many birthdays to celebrate, which means running around as well. The hou…

This week note covers the week of 29th June–5th July.

Life#
Last week I got back to work after a week’s break. And work I did! I switched my office cab time from 7:30 AM to 9:30 AM so that I could sleep a little longer. Now I have breakfast at home instead of office, and I start working right from the cab so that I get to work same amount of time. I’ve been sleeping 10+ hours every night and it is finally working! I feel much better than a few weeks ago, almost back to my normal health.
I’ve noticed that HRV is a good overall indicator of my health. The following chart shows my weekly average HRV over the last one month, as captured by my smartwatch:



You can see how it slowly went down over the first two weeks and then started to go back up over the last two weeks. It’s still not back …

The day after IndieWebClub Bangalore Special Anniversary Meetup, Ankur, Tanvi and I got together and did a retrospective on the event. We noted down what went well, what didn’t, and what we should do the next time. This note summarizes our discussion.
What Went Well#
We front-loaded many decisions, such as talk format, venue, date, topics etc., and didn’t second-guess them. This helped us later with our tight schedule.
We were serious about the CFP from the get-go. We wrote a detailed CFP statement and made a web page for it. This made participants also take it seriously. We actively reached out to folks from the community asking them to submit proposals. Most of our proposals came from the people we reached out to.

articles.description:
This week note covers the week of 22nd–28th June.

Life#
I took the whole last week off to recover from illness and fatigue. I’m happy to report that all three of us are doing much better now. I had a sinus infection, not major, but enough to give me headaches entire days. Thankfully, the medication worked, and now I’m almost over it.
Earlier I had decided to not work on personal projects last week, but as I started feeling better, I couldn’t resist it. I worked on them for two days out of seven, which I consider pretty good knowing myself. I spent the rest of the time reading and watching TV, going for walks, and generally resting. I slept 10–11 hours each day. I finally feel rested enough.
Last Monday I weighed myself as usual, and found myself to be at my lowest in many decades. However…

articles.description:
Happy July 4th!  For those of us around the world contemplating
independence, it's a good day to think about how we came to rely on
expensive cloud infrastructure for our fundamental computing needs.
With that in mind, here is my latest toy project: an open source tool that
makes replicating, forking, sharing, and running container snapshots fast
and easy across cloud and personal devices.
It's fun to play with, especially on bare metal hardware you run at home, or
rent from a provider like Hetzner or OVH. Or, because it uses Tailscale, why
not all of them in a single mesh?
There's a lot more to say but I don't have time right now. Details are in
the README.
I will say this: humans and AI agents both want the same things when they're
trying to get work done.  Ephemeral containers aren't really it.  But how
about unlimited disk space, fast CPUs, an undo button, and the ability to
move to whatever provider offers the best hardware at the best price? 
That's more like it.
Go visit thundersnap on github
and tell me what you think!
articles.title: thundersnap 0.01: an undo button for everything
